step-1.text: Lay one side panel flat, holes facing up. Screw in two cam pins and tap in two wood dowels.

count-1.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 2 cam pins and 2 wood dowels.

step-2.text: Push the bottom panel onto the low pins and dowels. Drop two cam locks into the round holes, arrows facing the pins, and turn them clockwise until they grab.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 bottom panel and 2 cam locks.

step-3.text: Tap dowels into the panel below, then press the divider down onto them. Dowels go in the top end too, ready for what sits above.

count-3.text: This step uses 1 divider and 4 wood dowels.

step-4.text: Pins and dowels go into the ends of the panels on this side too. With a helper, lower the second side onto all of them at once, then lock the last two cam locks.

count-4.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 2 cam pins, 2 wood dowels and 2 cam locks.

step-5.text: Tap four dowels into the top edges of the sides. Set the top panel on, good side up, then lock it from inside with four cam locks.

count-5.text: This step uses 1 top panel, 4 wood dowels and 4 cam locks.

step-6.text: Tap four dowels into the ends of the plinth board and press it in under the bottom panel, at the front.

count-6.text: This step uses 1 plinth and 4 wood dowels.

step-7.text: Roll the wardrobe over so it lies on its front. Ask your helper, and put the flattened box underneath to save the finish.

count-7.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-8.text: Lay the back panel on, smooth side facing in. Line it up with the bottom corners and nail it along the edges, about every twenty centimeters. If the corners line up, the wardrobe is square.

step-9.text: Second back piece, butted tight against the first. Same nailing pattern along every edge.

step-10.text: Stand it up together. Lift with your legs, not your back.

count-10.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-11.text: The shelf above the rail goes in first, high up. Push four shelf pins into the holes at the height you want for each shelf, twenty pins in all, then rest the shelves on them, front edge flush.

count-11.text: This step uses 5 shelves and 20 shelf pins.

step-12.text: Screw a rail holder to each side of the hanging space, level with each other, then drop the clothes rail into the holders. Hang one coat and check it slides freely.

count-12.text: This step uses 1 clothes rail, 2 rail holders and 4 screws.

step-13.text: Press four hinges into the round cups on the back of each door, twelve in all, then clip each door onto its mounting plates inside the frame. The mirror door is heavier and breakable: carry it upright and hang it last. Doors this tall need a second pair of hands.

count-13.text: This step uses 2 doors, 1 mirror door, 12 hinges and 24 screws.

step-14.text: Close every door and look at the gaps. The screws on each hinge move a door up, down, in and out. A quarter turn at a time until the gaps are even and the doors meet in a straight line.

count-14.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-15.text: Last and most important. A full wardrobe with an open door can tip forward. Fix the wall bracket to the top at the back, then screw it into the wall with fixings that suit your wall. Always anchor it.

done.text: Done. Your BRIMNES wardrobe with 3 doors is built. Give it a proud little pat.
